papers.title: Substrate-dependent friction and climbing performance in a flying snake
papers.summary: Locomotion in limbless animals depends on friction between the body and substrate. In snakes, the skin-substrate interface can generate frictional anisotropy, lowering resistance during forward motion while increasing resistance during backward or transverse motion. These properties have inspired models and robots that rely on directional friction, yet empirical measurements remain limited across species and substrates. papers.summary: Understanding how birds encode object color is fundamental to elucidating the neural mechanisms of color vision. papers.title: Controlled flight of an insect-scale flapping-wing robot via integrated onboard sensing and computation
papers.summary: Aerial insects can effortlessly navigate dense vegetation, whereas similarly sized aerial robots typically depend on offboard sensors and computation to maintain stable flight. This disparity restricts insect-scale robots to operation in motion-capture environments, substantially limiting their applicability to tasks such as search-and-rescue operations and precision agriculture. In this work, we present a 1.29-gram aerial robot capable of hovering and tracking trajectories with solely onboard sensing and computation. papers.title: Manufacturing Dark Green Religion in the European Ecovillage Milieu
papers.summary: Ecovillages in Europe are places of embodied and performed dark green religion (DGR) where the gap between environmental values and behavior highlighted by Yi-Fu Tuan in 1970 may, at least in part, be narrowed. Ecovillages may also enable the human animal to better adapt to its habitats, in part due to DGR worldviews and the dwelling practices informed by various of its nature reverencing spiritualities.
